name: Imagine
what: A place made of column pages: a hub rail shows four grouped categories of sections, each opening as a column beside the rail in one row.
parts: Default Start column with card previews
features: Column-based navigation opens sections in the same row
Grouped sections (Tools, Worlds, Shapes, Studies) organize the 24 pages
State remembered by URL using page.store()
One crumb strip for the entire hierarchy
Depth 1 prevents expensive page loads

demos.shows: The hub itself with rail navigator and Start card wall showing grouped sections

gaps: How state persistence works across reloads
Deep nesting three levels down (e.g. person->board->task)
Interaction with child pages (team, game, gallery)
blurb: Column host with grouped rail, one row, four categories.

name: Scenes
what: A 3D pager where the page tree is the scene graph; clicking objects in the canvas navigates to different 3D worlds with live miniature previews on portal doors.
parts: Five grain variations (world, object, region, light, all)
features: Click 3D objects to navigate between scenes
Swap different parts of the scene (world, object, region, light, all together)
Take a guided tour with automatic navigation and timeline cues
Portal doors show live previews of their contents
Fog, lighting, and camera control per scene

demos.shows: The foyer rotunda with five portal doors and live miniature previews
Automatic navigation through all five grains of swap

gaps: Detailed slot mechanism and diff algorithm
Why random numbers must use stage.rand() instead of Math.random()
Aspect ratio and FOV widening behavior on ultrawide screens
blurb: 3D pager: page tree is scene graph, click objects to navigate.

stage.should_cap: No, full bleed is correct for 3D canvas.

name: Stream
what: A page edited in one browser tab appears live in every other tab within 9 ms, using append-only deltas streamed over a socket from a JSONL log.
features: Edit a page's state in one window and see it live in others
Append-only deltas with set/del/append operations
Reload preserves state from snapshot plus all deltas
Compact operation folds log back into snapshot
Clear operation discards log and reverts to snapshot

demos.shows: Two independently subscribed windows on the same data, one showing edits live in the other
Interactive wire demo where users can edit state
Streamed slide deck with live updates
Streamed region demo with live editing

gaps: Why editors must not apply their own edits before the server confirms
Offline behavior (socket degrades to fetch on non-localhost)
How hidden tabs handle the lack of requestAnimationFrame
blurb: Edit in one tab, live in every other, no reload.

stage.should_cap: No, wide layout suits the hero card with two windows.

name: Team
what: A roster rail of six team members, where selecting a person shows their task board with draggable cards organized by four lanes, state remembered across reloads.
parts: Person column with profile and assignments
Board with four lanes (Queued, In hand, Review, Landed)
Draggable task chips with point counts
features: Drag tasks between lanes with visual feedback
Switch between density (comfy/compact) views
Sort tasks by name or load
Board follows person selection
State persisted in localStorage with one key per page URL

demos.shows: The full roster, board, and draggable task interface in one view

gaps: How page.store() keys work with localStorage
The role of this.topic() for cross-column communication
Why Draggable.under() filter is needed to avoid landing on chips
blurb: Roster, boards, draggable tasks remembered by URL.

stage.should_cap: No, measured columns are appropriate here.

name: Vary
what: Four labs showing column-page layout variations across four questions: scroll behavior, background hierarchy, child display method, and column styling looks.
parts: Place lab with child display methods
Colstyles lab with four looks (Finder, Cards, Ink, Glass)
features: Browse variations visually in a card wall
Click a card to view the full variation page
See one-line verdict at the end of each variation
Compare different styling approaches side by side
Test how columns behave at different widths

demos.shows: Preview wall with four labs, each showing 3-4 variations
Scrollbar variations including full bleed edge case
How children get displayed in column pages
Four visual looks on the same tree structure

gaps: Why width: full collapses /imagine/'s own sidebar
The CSS rules and container query logic behind each lab
Performance implications of different styling approaches
blurb: Four labs: scroll, tone, place, four column looks.

stage.should_cap: No, wide layout fits all four preview cards in one row at 3440.

name: YouTube
what: Six labs demonstrating the YouTube IFrame Player API and a timeline cue engine that drives different UI patterns without loading iframes until play is pressed.
features: Lazy-load YouTube iframes only on play
Drive UI with timeline cue engine at 4x per second
Mark video boundaries with M key and copy array
Multiple UI patterns on the same video and engine
Keyboard controls (Space, arrows, J/L, M, 0-9)

demos.shows: Control panel interface driving video playback
Chapter navigation mode automatic or manual
Video scaled and translated with aside content
Split layout with video and synchronized content

gaps: Why backward scrub replays every cue from the start
Hidden tab behavior with polling and requestAnimationFrame
Container query reordering in panel for narrow widths
blurb: Six API labs: panel, course, yield, split, chat, marks.

stage.should_cap: No, wide layout suits the video and control panels.
